summary: Shaikh Ali Mashhour continues his discussion of Zadul-Ma'ad by addressing scholarly disagreements regarding the nature of the Prophet Muhammad's Night Journey and Ascension (Isra and Mi'raj). He clarifies that while scholars have differed on whether the journey involved both body and soul or only the soul, all companions and the majority of scholars agree it was a physical and spiritual event—not merely a dream vision. The Prophet experienced physical changes, such as his heart being washed in Zamzam, leaving visible scars witnessed by companions. Shaikh Ali emphasizes that miracles transcend normal physical laws and should not be rationalized through conventional understanding. He then pivots to an important methodological point: not all scholarly differences of opinion carry equal weight. Using examples like the requirement to recite Surah Al-Fatihah in prayer, he illustrates that the Quran and Sunnah are generally clear on essential matters, and when scholarly differences exist, some opinions are stronger than others based on evidence. He cautions against the false belief that differing opinions make all interpretations equally valid, comparing the relationship between the Quran/Sunnah and scholarly interpretation to seeing the Kaaba directly versus needing a compass when it is obscured.
suggested_title: The Nature of Isra and Mi'raj: Miracle, Scholarly Consensus, and the Weight of Differing Opinions
catchy_title: When Scholarly Differences Don't Mean All Opinions Are Equal
